title: Financial services — deprioritize unless specific sub-use-case
floras_mechanism: Investment banks, asset managers, and capital markets firms are generally a poor primary fit for Floras' supplier-embedded, high-volume goods procurement model. Their operations are services-heavy with limited supplier networks for physical inputs. Exceptions may exist—corporate travel programs, card or lending product innovation, financed emissions programs—but default outreach should deprioritize unless research surfaces a specific, credible transaction path. Do not conflate financial services ESG activity with Floras core ICP.
pain_signals: services-heavy business model with minimal goods procurement
ESG focus on financed emissions or portfolio—not supplier transactions
high revenue but low transaction-embed surface for physical goods
climate strategy centered on lending standards or portfolio alignment
buyer_personas: Innovation or product lead (cards/lending only if applicable)
budget_source: ESG program budget; corporate travel budget; sustainable finance product budget (only for specific product-led exceptions)
safe_claims: Floras' core model targets transaction-embedded climate value in procurement and supplier relationships
Financial services firms are typically lower fit for supplier-embedded Floras unless a specific sub-use-case applies
Corporate travel or product-led programs (cards, loans) may be evaluated separately from generic financial services outreach
conditional_claims: If the firm has significant corporate travel or private aviation, evaluate the corporate travel case pattern separately
If the firm issues consumer or commercial card products, evaluate the credit card rewards case pattern
If the firm offers green loan products, evaluate the sustainable loan case pattern
avoid_claims: Floras fits investment banks because they have large revenues
Financial services ESG leadership implies high Floras fit
Floras addresses financed emissions or portfolio decarbonization directly
Every bank should adopt supplier-embedded Floras

output_templates.one_liner: {company_name} is likely a low-priority Floras target unless a specific travel or product use case applies.
output_templates.short_pitch: {company_name} operates in financial services where climate strategy typically centers on portfolios, financed emissions, or lending standards—not high-volume goods procurement. Floras' core strength is embedding climate value into supplier and purchasing transactions, which is a weak default fit here. Deprioritize broad outreach unless research shows a credible exception such as significant corporate travel, card rewards innovation, or green lending products worth a targeted conversation.

objections_and_responses.objection: We're a major global bank with ambitious net-zero goals.
objections_and_responses.response: Net-zero ambition in financial services often targets financed emissions and portfolio alignment—a different problem than transaction-embedded supplier Floras. Fit should be assessed on specific spend categories and product lines, not headline climate commitments.

objections_and_responses.objection: Our employees travel extensively for client work.
objections_and_responses.response: Significant corporate travel may justify evaluating the corporate travel Floras pattern as a separate, narrower conversation—not a general financial services supplier pitch.

objections_and_responses.objection: We want to be seen as an ESG innovator.
objections_and_responses.response: Floras product-led cases (cards, green loans) may apply where the firm issues those products. Generic investment banking outreach on supplier embed is unlikely to resonate and risks misaligned positioning.
